read_population.measured_via: report.json read_population: every paged read (episodes and edges, per graph) through graphiti_client._paged_ro_query reported complete=true, with the edge census as count(r)

notes: graphiti_core version 0.28.2, as reported by importlib.metadata.version("graphiti-core") in this worktree's .venv.
report.json is the file the script wrote with --out-dir (json.dumps(indent=2, sort_keys=True)); it was not hand-edited.

EDGE CENSUS FIX BEFORE ANY ARTIFACT RUN (commit a9e1bdf1ad): the first worksheet run used MATCH (a)-[r:RELATES_TO]->(b) RETURN count(*), which FalkorDB evaluates as distinct connected (a, b) node PAIRS when r is unreferenced (dark_factory 19,409 vs count(r) = count(DISTINCT r.uuid) = 20,491; WITH DISTINCT a, b also returns 19,409). That read was complete (rows_seen equalled the true edge count) but the census could not have caught a truncation of up to the multi-edge excess. Every run since, including this one, uses count(r) and reports rows_seen == expected_rows.

SAMPLE STABILITY: the 48-episode / 291-minted-edge sample drawn by the pre-registration worksheet run (before the fix and again after it) is the sample this run re-derived; load_verdicts found 0 missing, 0 out-of-sample and 0 stale verdicts.

LIVE CORPUS: both graphs were being written during the run (episodes 8,700 at the pre-registration run vs 8,717 here); population counts are a snapshot at swept_at. The frozen sample window ends 2026-10-01T00:00Z, so later writes do not move the sample.
READ-ONLY: the script issued only GRAPH.RO_QUERY via _paged_ro_query; it has no mutation flag and its tests run it against a double whose query() raises.
